title: Forensic archive retention and query playbook (approval lifecycle + sample payloads)
content:
Goal:
This doc is a working PRD-style playbook for how we store, index, query, and present customer-managed private deployment audit artifacts for the purposes of approvals, post-incident forensics, and compliance. It focuses on retention scenarios, sample archived payloads (what a unit of evidence looks like), query access patterns, and lightweight explainability fields to speed triage.

Context and motivation:
- Customers deploying Redwood Private ask for auditable, queryable evidence when operators make network or model roll changes.
- Our approval gates currently emit minimal logs; customers need richer artifacts to reconstruct decisions and to prove non-repudiation during audits.
- We must balance retention cost vs forensics fidelity (full payloads vs compact proofs).

Principles:
1) Minimal viable evidence: retain the smallest set of fields that allow a reviewer to replay decision context and outcome.
2) Query-first organization: index artifacts by approval id, actor, change type, resource, and trace id so common queries are fast.
3) Immutable envelope: each archived artifact is signed by an operator identity (or KMS signature) and includes a canonical hash for integrity checks.
4) Retention tiers: fast hot window for short-term investigations; cold archive for long-tail audits.

Primary user stories:
- As a security auditor, I want to search all approval events for customer X between two dates and filter by resource (VPC/VPN/firewall) so I can sample for audit evidence.
- As a SRE, I want to retrieve the exact approval payload and the operator-signed certificate for a rollback that occurred 90 days ago.
- As a customer, I want to export the approval timeline for my tenant as a zipped bundle for my internal audit.

Artifact schema (sketch) - one artifact per approval/change bundle (stored as JSON or compacted protobuf):
- artifact_id: string (uuid)
- approval_id: string
- tenant_id: string
- resource: string (e.g., cust-vpc-123)
- change_type: string (firewall-rule-add, route-modify, operator-rollback)
- actor: string (operator@redwood or delegated-admin@cust)
- timestamp: iso8601
- decision: string (approved | rejected | auto-failover)
- reason_summary: string (short freeform)
- decision_explain: string (structured bullet or short NLP extract of why) -- optional
- signed_blob: base64 (operator-signed envelope, includes original request + metadata)
- hash: sha256 hex
- related_traces: list of trace ids (for correlating with observability)
- attached_evidence_refs: list of storage keys (for larger artifacts like pcap or syslogs)
- retention_tier: string (hot-30d | warm-365d | cold-archive)
- size_bytes: number (stringified number in bytes)

NOTE: Because Google Drive docs must be readable, above is a simplified JSON sketch. The actual storage format may be protobuf or avro, see linked artifacts.

Sample archived payload (example encoded form - human readable variant):
{
  "artifact_id": "a1b2c3-...",
  "approval_id": "APP-2026-00088",
  "tenant_id": "cust-omega",
  "resource": "edge-gateway-12",
  "change_type": "route-modify",
  "actor": "operator:jonas.erickson@redwood",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-20T16:12:33Z",
  "decision": "approved",
  "reason_summary": "customer requested route for internal BGP peering to allow egress to region-eu-1",
  "decision_explain": "operator annotated: validated peering acl, no overlap with reserved subnets, automated smoke test passed",
  "signed_blob_ref": "s3://forensic-archive/cust-omega/APP-2026-00088/signed.json",
  "hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "related_traces": ["trace-8bcf"],
  "attached_evidence_refs": ["s3://forensic-archive/cust-omega/APP-2026-00088/packet-capture.pcap"],
  "retention_tier": "warm-365d",
  "size_bytes": "42102"
}

Retention scenarios (cost v fidelity):
- Hot-30d (default): full signed_blob + decision_explain + attachments indexes. Kept on low-latency storage for immediate queries and can be returned via Console/export in <2s for typical payloads under 100KB.
- Warm-365d: signed_blob compressed (gzip) + derivation proofs (hashes), attachments removed but stored as cold references. Queries return summary and links to request retrieval (48-72h retrieval SLA).
- Cold-7y-archive: only compacted provenance record (artifact_id, approval_id, hash, retention_policy, admin_signature) stored in immutable ledger. Retrieval is manual, queued, and costs apply.

Query patterns and sample queries to optimize (Console + API):
- "List approvals for tenant X between dateA and dateB" -> should hit time + tenant index.
- "Show approval by approval_id" -> full artifact retrieval.
- "Search approvals by resource and change_type last 90d" -> resource index + change_type filter.
- "Find approvals where automated checks failed but decision approved" -> boolean on smoke_test_passed==false AND decision==approved (we should expose these structured fields).

Query performance notes:
- Keep the hot index denormalized for tenant-first access; many customer queries are scoped to a single tenant.
- Avoid full text scanning for typical UI flows. Provide a separate long-search job for coarse-grain investigations.
- Consider storing a compact vector (embedding) of decision_explain for similarity-based search of related decisions (helps auditors find precedent).

Approval gate UX / API considerations:
- API should return a query token for long-running retrievals (when pulling from warm/cold storage). Token includes retrieval ETA, cost estimate, and required authorizer roles.
- Console should allow a reviewer to see: timeline, raw signed blob (download), explainability bullets, and an index of related observability traces.
- Exports should be zipped bundles signed by our KMS and include a small README manifest that documents the retention tier.

Integrity and non-repudiation:
- Each artifact must include an operator signature (KMS) and a content hash stored in an immutable ledger (append-only, tamper-evident).
- Retention workflow must support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for customers with additional compliance needs.

Access control / least privilege:
- Default: only tenant admins and Redwood security hold short-term read access to hot artifacts.
- Escalation: SREs can request time-limited access tokens for forensics; requests are gated and logged as separate artifacts.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
1) Duration bands: is warm 365d a hard requirement or should we make this configurable per tenant? (ops cost vs compliance needs)
2) Attachment handling: full pcap retention is expensive — should we store only rolling digests plus an on-demand snapshot?
3) Immutable ledger implementation: use lightweight merkle-chained blobs in our DB or integrate with a customer-provided ledger?
4) Explainability verbosity: store short NLP extract only or full operator notes?

Operational runbook (sketch):
- Day 0: artifact created at approval; hot-index write + signed_blob persisted.
- Day 1-30: frequent reads supported; cost billing on per-artifact size.
- Day 31: artifact evaluation job moves to warm tier (compress, unlink attachments). Update retention_tier field.
- Archive job (on schedule): compact provenance record + write ledger pointer, then clear cold storage after customer retention TTL.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- Ingestion SLO: 99.9% approval artifacts ingested within 1s of action.
- Hot-read SLO: 99% of approval lookups under 150ms for payloads <100KB.
- Warm retrieval SLA: 48h typical, 72h max. Costs surfaced to customer before retrieval.

Security & compliance notes:
- All artifacts encrypted at rest with tenant scoping keys.
- Access to exports audited and retained separately for at least 180 days.
- GDPR: provide tenant data export and deletion semantics tied to artifact retention policy.

Implementation checklist (MVP):
- [ ] canonical artifact schema finalized (small set of required fields)
- [ ] hot index implementation (tenant, approval_id, resource, change_type, timestamp)
- [ ] signing integration (KMS + optional BYOK path)
- [ ] retention job that transitions artifacts across tiers
- [ ] Console views for timeline, download, and export workflow
- [ ] API endpoints for search and retrieval with retrieval tokens
- [ ] cost model for warm/cold retrieval surfaced in Console

Next steps / owners:
- Maya T: consolidate this playbook into an actionable PRD for eng (target Jan 2026 roadmap).
- Omar R: prototype hot index + sample queries (POC due 4 weeks).
- Leah G: validate compliance requirements with legal for 7-year cold retention scenarios.
- Jonas E: sketch signed_blob format and KMS flow.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally high-level and tradeoff-oriented. Please comment inline with concrete constraints (e.g., max object size for hot reads, expected pcap retention percentage).
- I expect this doc to diverge from existing approval sketches by emphasizing retention tiers and query UX first (not storage binary).

End of doc.
